X.|OF THE APOSTLES.|319}}</noinclude>frendes. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=25}}† And it came to passe, Vvhen Peter vvas come in, Cornelius came to meete him, and falling at his feete {{sup|‖}} adored. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=26}}† But Peter lifted him vp saying, Arise, my self also am a man. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=27}}† And talking vvith him, he vvent in, and findeth many that vvere assembled, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=28}}† and he said to them, You knovv hovv abominable it is for a man that is a Ievve, to ioyne, or to approche vnto a stranger: but God hath shevved to me, to call no man common or vncleane. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=29}}† For the vvhich cause, making no doubt, I came vvhen I vvas sent for. I demaund therfore, for vvhat cause you haue sent for me? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=30}}† And Cornelius said, Foure daies since, vntil this houre, I vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ At the time of praier specially God sendeth men comfortable visitations.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''In the Greeke, fasting & praying''.}}∷ praying the ninthe houre in my house, and behold {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note these apparitions and visions to S. Peter, Cornelius, and others, in the Scriptures very oftē, against the incredulity of our Heretikes, that vvil beleeue neither vision nor miracle, not expressed in Scripture: these being beleeued of Christian men euē before they vvere vvritten.}}∷ a man stoode before me in vvhite apparel, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=31}}† and said: Cornelius, thy praier is heard, and thy almes-deedes are in memorie in the sight of God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=32}}† Send therfore to Ioppé, and call hither Simon that is surnamed Peter: he lodgeth in the house of Simon a tanner by the sea side. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=33}}† Immediatly therfore I sent to thee: and thou hast done vvel in comming. Novv therfore al vve are present in thy sight, to heare al things vvhatsoeuer are commaunded thee of the Lord.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=34}}† And Peter opening his mouth, said, In very deede I perceiue that God is not an accepter of persons. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=35}}† but in euery nation, he that feareth him, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not such as beleeue only, but such as feare God and vvorke iustice, are acceptable to him.}}∷ vvorketh iustice, is acceptable to him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=36}}† The word did God send to the children of Israël, preaching peace by {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} (this is Lord of al.) {{verse|chapter=10|verse=37}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 4, 12.''}}* You knovv the vvord that hath been made through al Ievvrie, for {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Epistle vpō Munday in Easter vveeke.}}∷ beginning from Galilee, after the baptisme vvhich Iohn preached. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=38}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth hovv God anointed him vvith the holy Ghost and vvith povver, vvho vvent through out doing good and healing al that vvere oppressed of the Deuil, because God vvas vvith him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=39}}† And vve are vvitnesses of al things that he did in the countrie of the Ievves and in Hierusalem, vvhom they killed hanging him vpon a tree. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=40}}† Him God raised vp the third day and {{sup|‖}} gaue him to be made manifest, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=41}}† not to al the people, but to vs, vvho did eate and drinke vvith him after he rose againe from the dead. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=42}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō Munday in vvhitsōvveeke.}}And he commaunded vs to preach to the people, and to testifie that it is he that of God vvas appointed iudge of the liuing and of the dead. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=43}}† To him al the prophets giue testimonie, that al receiue remission of sinnes by his name, vvhich beleeue in him.⊣<noinclude>{{rh|||As}}</noinclude>
